texts.li: {X_nameDef}, a traveler of {FACTION}, stopped {A_nameDef} in the yard and said a name {A_nameDef} hasn't used in years. {X_nameDef} remembers the face from the wanted posters, from when {A_nameDef} was {TALE}, and remembers the reward on it.\n\n{X_nameDef} would forget all about it for {COUNT} silver.

[lowtech] "It was a good likeness," {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} told {A_nameDef}, once they were alone. "The price under it was better."\n\nThe notice went up years ago, when {A_nameDef} was {TALE}. {X_nameDef} would forget ever seeing it, for {COUNT} silver.

[!lowtech] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} spent a long time looking at {A_nameDef} across the yard before coming over. {X_nameDef} has seen that face on a bounty list, from when {A_nameDef} was {TALE}, and thinks keeping it off the comms is worth {COUNT} silver.

li.label: Pay {X_objective} {COUNT} silver
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} pockets the silver, nods to {A_nameDef} and leaves before supper.

li.label: Call the bluff (they may talk)
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} gets no silver, shrugs, and goes on {X_possessive} way. So far that seems to be the end of it.
li.riskOutcome: {X_nameDef} gets no silver, and takes it badly. By the end of the week, all of {FACTION} will know what {A_nameDef} used to be.

li.label: Let {A_nameDef} talk to {X_objective}
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} takes {X_nameDef} for a long walk around the fields. Whatever is said out there, {X_nameDef} comes back pale and leaves without asking for anything.
li.riskOutcome: {A_nameDef} and {X_nameDef} talk behind the storehouse, and it goes badly. {X_nameDef} leaves in a hurry, promising that {FACTION} will hear about it.

remembered.li: [quiet] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} knows what {A_nameDef} used to be, and has kept quiet so far.
[talked] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} told {X_possessive} people what {A_nameDef} used to be.

texts.li: The seal on the letter is an old unit badge, and {A_nameDef} knew it before the letter was open. It's from {X_nameDef}, who commanded {A_objective} once.\n\n"I'm fighting {ENEMY} for {FACTION} these days, and we're short of everything but stubbornness. If your people can spare {TALE}, send it back with my rider. Win or lose, you'll hear from me, and if we win you'll have a share of the spoils."

[lowtech] {X_nameDef}, who was {A_nameDef}'s captain once, leads the fighters of {FACTION} against {ENEMY} now, and the campaign has run short. The letter a rider brought asks for {TALE}, for old times' sake.\n\nA share of the spoils will come back to the colony, if they win.

[!lowtech] The message on the comms is signed {X_nameDef}, {A_nameDef}'s old commander, and reads like a field order.

{FACTION} engaged with {ENEMY}. Supplies short. Request {TALE}. Share of spoils to follow on success.

{A_nameDef} read it twice, and stood up straighter the second time.

li.label: Send {TALE} (they may lose)
li.outcome: The supplies go out with {FACTION}'s rider, along with a few lines in {A_nameDef}'s hand for {A_possessive} old commander.

li.label: Send good wishes only
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} writes back with good wishes and no supplies, and doesn't say much at supper.

coming.li: Word from {TALE}'s campaign against {ENEMY} is due in about {DAYS}.

done.li: [won,lowtech] "We broke their line," {TALE} writes, "and your supplies were in our bellies when we did it." {FACTION} have beaten {ENEMY} in the field, and the colony's share of the spoils came with the letter: {ITEM}.
[won,!lowtech] {FACTION}'s militia has driven {ENEMY} back, {TALE} reports, and the colony's supplies kept them going when it counted. A share of the spoils has come with the news: {ITEM}.

[lost] {TALE} has written from the field, briefly. The campaign against {ENEMY} went badly, and {FACTION} have fallen back to their own lands. The colony's supplies were well used, {TALE} writes, and won't be forgotten.

cancelled.li: No word has come back from {TALE}'s campaign, and with things as they are between the colony and {FACTION}, none will.

texts.li: [healer] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has walked a long way, with a slight hitch in {X_possessive} stride, to find {A_nameDef}. Years ago, when {A_nameDef} was still a healer by trade, {A_pronoun} set that leg and sat up three nights with the fever after. {X_nameDef} has brought a gift.

[doctor] "You won't remember me," {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} told {A_nameDef} at the gate, and at first {A_nameDef} didn't. Then it came back: a bad fever on the road, years ago, and a long night pulling {X_nameDef} through it.\n\n{X_nameDef} has brought a gift.

{X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has come to see {A_nameDef}, who once saved {X_possessive} life with a needle, a lamp and a long night. The gift {X_nameDef} brought is wrapped in good cloth, and was plainly saved up for.

li.label: Accept the gift
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} unpacks the gift for {A_nameDef} piece by piece, and won't hear a word against it.

li.label: Ask {X_objective} to stay on (may say no)
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} says yes before the question is finished, and asks {A_nameDef} where {X_pronoun} can sleep.
li.riskOutcome: {X_nameDef} would like nothing better, but there's family at home expecting {X_objective} back before the season turns. {X_nameDef} leaves the gift behind anyway.

li.label: Ask {X_objective} to spread the word
li.outcome: Every settlement on {X_nameDef}'s road home will hear about the colony's healer, {X_pronoun} promises, whether they ask or not. The neighbors will know {A_nameDef}'s name.

texts.li: [outlaw] Mending the lining of an old coat, {A_nameDef} found a map folded into the seam. {A_nameDef} drew it years ago, as {TALE}, to mark where a share of the takings was buried, and had forgotten it was there.\n\nThe place is a few days' travel from the colony. Whether the takings are still in the ground is another matter.

[soldier] In the bottom of an old kitbag, {A_nameDef} found a map from the war, with a supply cache marked on it in a hand {A_pronoun} doesn't recognize. The unit that buried it never came back for it, as far as {A_nameDef} knows.\n\nIt's a few days' travel from here.

[trader] {A_nameDef} found an old ledger at the bottom of a chest, and pressed between its pages a map from {A_possessive} trading days, with a stash of goods marked on it. It's a few days' travel, and {A_nameDef} never told anyone else where it was.

[noble] Among the few things {A_nameDef} brought from {A_possessive} family's house is a book of old estate maps. Tucked in the back is one {A_nameDef} had never noticed: an old lodge a few days' travel from the colony, with something marked beneath its cellar.

[scholar] Sorting through old notes, {A_nameDef} found a map copied from an archive years ago, of a ruin {A_pronoun} always meant to visit. It's a few days' travel from the colony, and the archive's notes say something was left there.
A cross in faded ink, a few days' travel from the colony, is all the old map in {A_nameDef}'s things has to say. {A_nameDef} can't remember who gave it to {A_objective}, or why {A_pronoun} kept it.

li.label: Follow it up
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} copies the old marks onto the colony's own map. Whoever goes will need to travel.

li.label: Keep it as a keepsake
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} folds the map back up along its old creases and puts it away with {A_possessive} things.

outcomes.li: [gone] {A_nameDef} compares the old map with the colony's own and can't make them agree. Whatever it marked isn't there any more.

texts.li: [fossil] {A_nameDef} came running in with a split stone held in both hands. Pressed into the inside is the shape of a shell, perfectly clear, from some sea that dried up long before anyone lived here.\n\n{A_nameDef} wants to know everything about it. {B_nameDef} knows more than most, if {B_pronoun} can spare the time.

[coin] {A_nameDef} dug an old coin out of the mud by the path, green with age, stamped with a face that none of the adults recognize.\n\n{A_nameDef} has polished it on {A_possessive} sleeve until it shines, and wants to know whose face it is. {B_nameDef} might be able to guess.

[skull] {A_nameDef} brought home a bird's skull from the woods, white and light as paper, and set it beside {A_possessive} plate at supper. {A_nameDef} wants to know what kind of bird it was and how it flew.\n\n{B_nameDef} has offered to look at it with {A_objective}.

[geode] {A_nameDef} cracked open a round gray stone by the stream and found it full of purple crystal inside. {A_nameDef} has shown it to every person in the colony at least twice.\n\n{B_nameDef} could explain how the crystals got in there.

[machine] {A_nameDef} pulled a scorched circuit board out of an old junk pile, with a tiny screen that still glows when it's tilted. "It's a robot's brain," {A_pronoun} told {B_nameDef}, very seriously.\n\n{B_nameDef} could take it apart with {A_objective} and find out what it really was.

li.label: Let {B_nameDef} study it with {A_objective}
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} and {A_nameDef} bend over it together, and {A_nameDef} comes away with a head full of questions and a page of drawings.

li.label: Let {A_objective} keep it
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} puts it on the shelf over {A_possessive} bed, and checks on it every morning.

li.label: Trade it ({COUNT} silver)
li.outcome: It sells for {COUNT} silver. {A_nameDef} hands it over without a word, and is very quiet for the rest of the day.

texts.li: [game] {PET_nameDef} came trotting back with {BEAST} hanging from {PET_possessive} jaws, and wouldn't put it down until {A_nameDef} came to look. Fresh meat for the pot, and a very pleased animal.

[herbs] {PET_nameDef} came back from the woods and dropped a muddy mouthful of healing herbs in {A_nameDef}'s lap, roots and all. {A_nameDef} is telling anyone who'll listen that {PET_nameDef} knew exactly what {PET_pronoun} was doing.

[purse] A small leather purse, chewed at one corner, is the latest thing {PET_nameDef} has brought home, and {PET_nameDef} wouldn't give it up until {A_nameDef} traded a bone for it. {COUNT} silver inside. Somewhere on the road, a traveler will be patting their pockets tonight.
[component] {PET_nameDef} dug something out of the scrap heap and carried it proudly to {A_nameDef}: a component, slightly chewed and still in working order.

[nothing] An old boot that belongs to no one in the colony now sits on {A_nameDef}'s shelf. {PET_nameDef} brought it in from the fields and laid it at {A_nameDef}'s feet like a trophy, and it seemed rude to throw it out.

[lowtech,other] {A_nameDef} struck wood while digging and uncovered an old chest bound in iron, its lock rusted solid. It's heavy, and something inside shifts when it's tilted.\n\n{B_nameDef} thinks the lock will give to patience and a thin pick. An axe would be quicker and might ruin what's inside. A rider of {FACTION} would pay {COUNT} silver for it as it is.

[!lowtech,other] Under {A_nameDef}'s shovel was the lid of a supply crate, stenciled with a word too faded to read. The keypad is dead and the seals are whole, so whatever is inside has been dry all this time.\n\n{B_nameDef} wants a go at opening it properly. A crowbar is quicker. {FACTION} would pay {COUNT} silver for it unopened.

[mining,other] Cutting into the hillside, {A_nameDef} broke into a small hollow with a crate in it, sealed, and set down as neatly as the day someone left it there.\n\n{B_nameDef} thinks the lock can be opened without breaking anything, or it could just be broken. If the colony would rather not know, {FACTION} will pay {COUNT} silver for it sealed.

[same] {A_nameDef} found an old sealed crate while digging outside, and has been fiddling with its lock ever since. With the best hands in the colony and an afternoon, {A_nameDef} thinks it will open clean.\n\nThe quick way is a hammer. {FACTION} would give {COUNT} silver for it sealed.

li.label: Let {B_nameDef} work the lock open
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} spends the afternoon on the lock.
li.riskOutcome: {B_nameDef} spends the afternoon on the lock.

li.label: Break it open (it may break what's inside)
Sell it sealed ({COUNT} silver)
li.outcome: A rider of {FACTION} pays {COUNT} silver for the crate and hauls it away, still sealed. The colony will never know what was in it.

outcomes.li: [careful,safe] {B_nameDef} spends the afternoon on the lock and opens it without a scratch. Everything inside is dry and whole: {ITEM}.
[careful,risk] {B_nameDef} gets the lock open cleanly, but the seal had failed years ago and most of what was inside has rotted. What's left: {ITEM}.
[broken,safe] A few good swings and the lid comes off. Inside: {ITEM}.
[broken,risk] The lid gives on the third blow, and so does a good deal of what was under it. What survived: {ITEM}.
